question: A 4-year-old girl is brought to the pediatrician by her parents for a 1-year history of gradual loss of speech and motor skills. Pregnancy and delivery were uncomplicated, and development was normal until the age of 3 years. Her parents say she used to run and speak in short sentences but now is only able to walk slowly and cannot form sentences. She avoids eye contact and constantly rubs her hands together. There are no dysmorphic facial features. Neurologic examination shows marked cognitive and communicative delay. She has a broad-based gait and is unable to hold or pick up toys on her own. Which of the following mutations is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's condition?

options.opa: Microdeletion of methyl-CpG binding protein 2 on X-chromosome
options.opb: CGG trinucleotide repeat in FMR1 gene on X-chromosome
options.opc: CTG trinucleotide repeat in DMPK gene on chromosome 19
options.opd: Partial deletion of long arm of chromosome 7
options.ope:
Partial deletion of short arm of chromosome 5
"

nodes: Peroxisome Biogenesis Disorder, Complementation Group G
paths: (Peroxisome Biogenesis Disorder, Complementation Group G)-CAUSES->(Neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease)-CAUSES->(Disease)-CAUSES->(Fragile X Syndrome)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: CGG trinucleotide repeat in FMR1 gene on X-chromosome -> Fragile X syndrome -> gradual loss of speech and motor skills -> cognitive and communicative delay -> 90%
CHAIN: Microdeletion of methyl-CpG binding protein 2 on X-chromosome -> Rett syndrome -> gradual loss of speech and motor skills -> cognitive and communicative delay -> 90%
enhanced_information: The most likely underlying cause of this patient's condition is a CGG trinucleotide repeat in the FMR1 gene on the X-chromosome, leading to Fragile X syndrome. This mutation is associated with gradual loss of speech and motor skills, cognitive and communicative delay, which aligns with the patient's presentation.
analysis: The core medical principle guiding this case is the recognition of Fragile X syndrome, a genetic disorder caused by a CGG trinucleotide repeat in the FMR1 gene on the X-chromosome. Fragile X syndrome is characterized by developmental regression, cognitive impairment, and motor skill decline, which align with the patient's symptoms. The enhanced information provided strongly supports this diagnosis as the most likely cause of the patient's condition.
